content: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) campus is situated in Bethesda, Maryland. Most of the institutes conduct their Divisions of Intramural Research on this campus, which is distributed across various buildings. The campus is geographically located between Old Georgetown Road to the west, Wisconsin Avenue to the east, West Cedar Lane to the north, and downtown Bethesda to the south. The National Naval Medical Center is positioned directly across Wisconsin Avenue. The Medical Center Metro stop is conveniently located just beyond the campus fence along Wisconsin Avenue. The Clinical Center, also known as Building 10, was inaugurated in 1953 and originally contained 540 beds, enabling clinical research activities. This facility was established in the aftermath of the unethical Nazi medical experiments conducted during World War II, and as a result, all research protocols at the NIH are subject to ethical review by a designated review board. The Bethesda campus comprises over fifty buildings, which are numbered sequentially based on the order of their construction. As a federal government facility that houses sensitive research, the Bethesda campus enforces stringent security measures to ensure the safety of its employees, patients, and visitors. Immediate access to the campus requires a Department of Health and Human Services identification card. Visitors must present a government-issued photo ID to obtain a pass, and their vehicles and/or persons are subject to inspection.
